terra.problem: Papa says he learned about checking names the hard way with mail, inventing a personal experience outside his established world.
The pit-and-bad-attitude joke does not follow the trapping comparison: digging a pit does not imply a bad attitude.
The verse says Judah stumbles, not that Judah is on the ground.
The text says the people do not find the LORD. Saying they got nothing for bringing the animals goes beyond that.
The verse does not mention the herds being stolen, but it does not say they were not stolen.
The commands name the horn, trumpet and battle cry, but do not say they occur in that time sequence.
The verse calls for a battle cry but does not say the fight is still ahead.
The text does not say the LORD proclaims this so the tribes will not be surprised.
The explanation is a generic correction and quotation with no distinct Papa Dorin voice.
The verse says the king cannot cure or heal the wound. Saying he is no help at all goes further.
The verse says they will admit their guilt and seek His face, but does not say admitting guilt happens first.
The explanation is a flat restatement of the answer without a distinctive Papa Dorin voice.
Using the sun's repeated rising as a reason not to limit His appearing to one time draws a conclusion about frequency that the verse does not give.
